properties.desc: Radioactive slag / slag-like material in historic fill. Gamma survey (Ludlum 2221) measured >10,000 cpm here vs 6,000–8,000 cpm site background; gamma/alpha spectroscopy identified uranium, thorium and radium as the contributing radionuclides. Delineated in the 2012 Revised RI (Figure 3) as a soil-excavation target — a soil/slag hot zone, not a groundwater plume.
properties.source: NYSDEC BCP C932150 Revised RI Report (ERM, 2012), Figure 3 & §3.2.7

properties.coord_precision: site marker for interspersed impacted slag; peak-gamma sub-area mapped separately near TP-03
properties.hazard: Radioactive slag: thorium, radium, uranium (Th-232 & U-238 decay chains)
properties.gamma_cpm: Hot spots generally 15,000-60,000 CPM; up to 120,000-170,000 CPM near the TP-03 cluster; historic peak 420,000 CPM (a football-sized surface slag piece, since removed)
properties.desc: Radioactive slag (TENORM) interspersed in surface soil/fill, mostly within 2 ft of grade. MARSSIM gamma survey (through 8/7/12) delineated five hot spots >16,000 CPM (670-1,507 m²); readings generally 15,000-60,000 CPM, reaching 120,000-170,000 CPM near the TP-03 test-pit cluster. A single football-sized surface slag piece read 420,000 CPM and was removed for analysis. Gamma-spec of slag detected Ra-226, Ra-228, Ac-228, Tl-208, Th-234 and U-235.
properties.source: Covanta/Praxair RI Report (LaBella, 2013), Gamma Walkover Survey (Appendix)
properties.hot_spots_16000cpm: Five delineated areas >16,000 CPM: 670, 835, 857, 1,507 and 630 m²
properties.survey: MARSSIM gamma walkover survey (LaBella RI, Fig 15) through 8/7/2012; Ra-226 scan MDC <3 pCi/g

properties.hazard: Highest-radioactivity slag concentration (Th-232 & U-238 decay chains)
properties.gamma_cpm: 120,000-170,000 CPM at this location (the TP-03 test-pit cluster). The site-wide peak of 420,000 CPM was recorded separately, in the northern rail-line area — see note on precision.
properties.coord_precision: TP-03 test-pit cluster centroid. The RI locates the 120,000-170,000 CPM readings here explicitly. The 420,000 CPM site peak was recorded in the northern portion of the site adjacent to the rail lines and its exact position is NOT stated in the text (it is plotted on RI Figure 13); it is reported here as a site-wide figure, not as a reading at this point.
properties.desc: Hottest radiological sub-area of the Covanta parcel. Per the LaBella RI (§7.3), gamma readings near the TP-03 test-pit cluster reached 120,000-170,000 CPM against a site background of 5,526-7,522 CPM. Separately, the site-wide peak measurement of 420,000 CPM (§7.2) was traced to a single football-sized piece of slag partially exposed at the ground surface in the northern rail-line area; that piece was removed from the site for laboratory analysis. This is the TENORM slag hot spot (thorium/radium/uranium).
properties.source: LaBella Associates, Remedial Investigation Report, Covanta 15-Acre Site (2013), Fig 15 & §7.2
